Subject: Proposed sunset-trigger definition + opt-out orchestration

Hi Sara / OliveTech procurement team —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. As we discussed, two items popped up that will impact the Order Form and MSA redlines we expect from your side: (1) the automatic renewal cadence for pilots converting to committed capacity, and (2) the termination-for-convenience (opt‑out) mechanics when service sunsetting is required.

To keep the review tidy, I attached a short table that maps: notice window -> business trigger -> operational handoff -> billing/escrow expectation. Please take a look and let us know if the mapping reflects how OliveTech treats staged commit transitions.

Proposed next steps:
- You review the attached table and confirm which rows reflect required notice windows for the various commitment tiers.
- If OliveTech needs a hard 60/90/120 day notice vs. a conditional trigger (e.g., 30 days after product EOL announcement), flag the preferred row.
- We’ll have our legal team (cc’d) propose language that matches your preference for the MSA and Order Form.

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for sending — useful framing. A couple of clarifying points from our procurement & product ops:

1) For pilot-to-commit transitions we typically want a 60-day notice window for any change to auto-renew behavior.
2) For product-level sunsets (when the vendor decommissions a feature), our SRE team expects at least 90 days notice plus a documented migration plan.
3) Regarding termination-for-convenience, we prefer a tiered approach where smaller pilots (< $25k TCV) can exit on 30 days, committed enterprise contracts need 90 days plus transition assistance.

I’ve attached a marked-up copy of your table with our suggested rows highlighted and a short redline doc for the MSA section where we added the 90-day requirement.

Attachment: [Attachment: OliveTech_redlines.docx (docx, 48KB)]

Can your legal team incorporate these into a proposed redline? We’d like to have an internal sign-off by the end of the week if possible.

—
Sara Lim
Senior Procurement Manager
OliveTech

Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed sunset-trigger definition + opt-out orchestration

Sara — appreciate the quick review and clear asks.

Summary of OliveTech requests (per your markup):
- Pilot auto-renew notice: 60 days
- Product sunset notice: 90 days + migration plan
- TFC (termination for convenience): tiered 30/90 day approach depending on TCV threshold

Rishi / Kim — can you review the attached redlines and propose concise MSA + Order Form language that: (a) captures the 60/90/30/90 windows above, (b) creates a fallback path for emergency security-driven sunset with shorter notice but defined remediation/credits, and (c) clarifies who covers migration runbook costs in a sunset?

Operational note for Ben: OliveTech expects a documented handoff to SRE when sunset is invoked (90d) and an optional escrow/bridge arrangement if migration exceeds 120 days. Ben — can you confirm whether a temporary credits program or escrow is acceptable commercially?

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-minute redline review tomorrow afternoon unless you prefer an earlier slot.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed sunset-trigger definition + opt-out orchestration

Lauren / team —

I reviewed OliveTech's markup. High level comments from Legal:

1) Notice windows: We can accept the 60/90/30/90 structure but need to add specific language that defines when notice is "given" (email to listed contacts + portal posting) and when it is "received" (business days after posting). That avoids disputes about ambiguous delivery mechanisms.

Suggested clause (short): "Notice shall be deemed given on the date of delivery to the recipient's designated email address or publication to the mutually-designated customer portal; receipt shall be deemed three (3) business days thereafter for cross-jurisdictional customers unless otherwise agreed in writing."

2) Emergency/SECURITY sunset: We will propose carveout language that allows Redwood to shorten notice for verified security incidents, subject to: (a) documented incident disclosure, (b) 100% credit for impacted usage days, and (c) cooperation on mitigation.

3) Migration / escrow: Redlines will offer two commercial paths — a time-limited credits program (default) or an escrowed transitional support fee (customer-paid) if migration extends beyond 120 days. We recommend keeping default to credits to avoid creating a perpetual escrow liability.

I’ll prepare a redline PDF with the proposed text and send to the thread by EOD.

Attachment: [Attachment: redline-msa-term-suggestions.pdf (pdf, 22KB)]

—
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracting

Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed sunset-trigger definition + opt-out orchestration

Sara — quick commercial response from our side.

- Credits program: Redwood can offer a time-limited credit equal to unused committed capacity pro-rated for days remaining when sunset is invoked. Credits are applied to future invoices for up to 12 months.
- Escrow option: We can accommodate a customer-funded escrow for multi-quarter migrations; Redwood prefers credits as default to keep ops simple.
- Migration runbook: We will provide an SRE-owned migration runbook template and a 2-week onboarding workshop at no charge for enterprise contracts > $250k.

If that aligns, Kimberly — feel free to fold the commercial language into the redline (credit terms, 12-month expiry, escrow optionality). Lauren — I’ll be available for the redline review tomorrow at 10am PT.

Thanks —
